subject: CHE
label: Grade 12 Science
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 12 Science Chemistry, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 6 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Solutions and electrochemistry
modules.outcome: calculate colligative properties and cell potentials
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Solutions and electrochemistry', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: calculate colligative properties and cell potentials. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Observe: see, touch, measure or watch a safe demonstration linked to 'Solutions and electrochemistry' and write what you notice.
Explain: use the key words of the unit to say what is happening and why, in a few lines.
Use it: calculate colligative properties and cell potentials. Use a diagram, table or short calculation where it fits.
Test and conclude: say what evidence supports your answer and what you would change.
modules.example: Solved: 10 g of salt in 90 g of water: solution mass 100 g, so concentration = 10 / 100 x 100 = 10 percent by mass. Method: Model run for 'Solutions and electrochemistry'. Question: what do we want to find out? Prediction: one sentence. Method: three safe steps with the equipment named. Record: a small table with units. Conclusion: one sentence that uses the evidence and the key words of the unit. What a good answer looks like: a fair test, measured values with units, and a conclusion that matches the table.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Calculate colligative properties and cell potentials: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Solutions and electrochemistry), and at which Bloom level is it?
'calculate', at the Apply level.
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 6 (Biomolecules and polymers) run?
Weeks 31 to 36.
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A timed paper and an error log. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: observe, sort and describe the living and non-living world.
L2: run simple tests and explain with key words.
L3: use models and equations; plan a fair test.
L4: link physics, chemistry and biology ideas with calculation.
L5: specialise; design, analyse and evaluate experiments.
L6 (degree): laboratory science, instrumentation and analysis.
L7 (postgraduate): research design and expert practice.
